core.title: Keep the cross-unit produce/consume graph acyclic
core.given: A plan's units (the composition units the profile names, each a bounded slice of the product) declare produce/consume entries by artifact NAME, forming a directed graph with an edge producer-unit -> consumer-unit whenever a name produced by one unit is consumed by another.
core.when: You author, edit or review any plan containing such units, whether or not your change touches produce/consume entries.
core.then: Ensure the name-keyed unit graph is acyclic: no strongly-connected component may contain more than one unit, including cycles that already existed.
prefer: Before adding an edge producer B -> consumer A (A consumes a name B produces), check by artifact name whether a path A -> B already exists; if it does, the new edge would close a cycle.
When a loop exists, restructure unit boundaries or artifact ownership so dependencies flow one way.
avoid: Reasoning about unit dependencies via the plan format's optional linkage field, when it has one, instead of the produce/consume artifact name; that field is nullable, so artifact names are the only reliable key.
Mutual or transitive produce/consume loops between two or more units.
Hiding a loop by nulling or renaming the optional linkage field while the artifact names still loop.
core.why: A cross-unit produce/consume cycle means no unit in the loop can be delivered before the others; the graph must be a DAG so units can be ordered. Artifact names are the only reliable key because the optional linkage field is nullable.
evidence: SCC analysis of the name-keyed unit graph (nodes = units, edges producer -> consumer by artifact name) reports no component with more than one unit.
verification: Generic check: nodes are the plan's units; add a directed edge producer-unit -> consumer-unit whenever an artifact NAME produced by one unit is consumed by another; run strongly-connected-component analysis and report every SCC containing more than one unit as a violation, whether pre-existing or newly introduced.
Edges are keyed on the produce/consume artifact name only, never on the plan format's optional linkage field.
Change-level attribution (whether the current change produced the entry that closed the cycle) only labels findings; it is not a precondition for firing, so pre-existing cycles are still violations.

fires: A planner adds a consume entry to unit A for an artifact name produced by unit B, while A already (directly or transitively) feeds B by artifact name.
A planner splits a unit and the two resulting units each consume an artifact name the other produces.
Two units have null or absent optional linkage fields but share produce/consume artifact names forming a loop.
A planner makes an unrelated edit (e.g. only to an optional linkage field) in a plan whose unit graph already contains a multi-unit SCC: the existing cycle is still a violation.
doesNotFire: A unit produces and consumes artifact names only internally (an SCC of size one unit).
Cross-unit produce/consume edges exist but form a DAG (e.g. A->B->C with no path back).
The work involves no units or produce/consume entries at all.

profileRequirements.meaning: What the stack calls the plan's composition unit — the bounded slice of the product that a plan decomposes work into and whose produce/consume artifact-name entries form the dependency graph; also the term matched in task/plan text for activation.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's local name/construct for the plan's composition unit: the bounded slice of the product that a plan decomposes work into, that plan artifacts are grouped under, and that declares the produce/consume artifact-name entries the dependency graph is keyed on.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: layout.wagon_dir gives only the source directory shape of one wagon and urn.wagon only a URN shape, but bun.json states neither; no existing key says what the stack calls the unit whose produce/consume graph the core constrains and whose term activation matches in task text. The roles params are closed and contain no plan-unit role.

neutralityNotes: The rule is otherwise fully stack-neutral: it constrains only the plan's declared name-keyed produce/consume graph, with no code, path, suffix or tooling content. (1) 'wagon' is generalized to the plan's composition unit ('unit') and instantiated per stack through the proposed key idiom.plan_unit (Bun: wagon); the vocabulary knows a wagon's directory (layout.wagon_dir) and URN shape (urn.wagon) but not the unit term itself, and bun.json contains no path or URN value to bind those keys to. (2) 'contract field' is generalized to 'the plan format's optional linkage field'; its Bun name and corpus-wide nullability stay with the realization (bunOnly). In a stack whose plan format has no such field, the field clauses of avoid[0]/avoid[2] and the last sentence of why are vacuous and the name-keying acyclicity obligation stands unchanged, so the core is neither weaker nor stronger. (3) The finding/term id consume_cycle and the detector reference are realization details kept in bunOnly; per-rule severity 3 and strict disposition are carried in core:verification, not the profile.
